doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Naomi Campbell, Hugo Chavez, Castro at Birdland and the Theresa Hotel
summary: Jones talks about Naomi Campbell as a daughter, a call from Hugo Chavez, meeting Castro at Birdland after the revolution, the Theresa Hotel, Ron Brown and Malcolm X.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: It’s awesome. It’s funny, because Naomi Campbell’s like my daughter, 16 years. Mandela’s her grandpoppy. I’m poppy. She’s the sweetest girl in the world, but boy, she can do it. She’s always into something. “Poppy” – she’s a writer now, one of the editorial staff for GQ. “Poppy.” “Yes baby?” “Somebody wants to talk to you.” It’s Hugo Chavez. She’s dating his son, right. He says, “You’ve got to come down.” I met Castro at

Birdland two weeks after the revolution. Pee Wee Marquette – he’s staying at the Theresa – Pee Wee Marquette said, “Hey, you all better not mess with me. Better tip me more, because Castro said when the atomic bomb comes in, they’re not going to hit the Theresa Hotel.” Castro was a nice guy then.
I remember when you cooked the chicken in the room.
I cooked the chicken. Ron Brown was raised at the Theresa.
Yeah. He was raised. His father was the manager.
I used to stand out in front of that many times listening to Malcolm. I was so glad again, in light of the diaspora, your references to Malcolm X in the book. I found them very touching, very moving.
He was something else. Detroit Red. And his daughter, Atallah Shabazz, is an incredible human being.
